summary.intent: Check on the state of the Callisto repo after a usage-limit block (conflicting PRs, Codex's work, local-only branches), decide how to recover the unpublished 0.15.0 release, and review Codex's merged changes for defects.
summary.outcome: Confirmed all PRs merged with main green, cleaned local worktrees/branches (28 to 4 worktrees, 111 to 6 branches, unproven tips archived under refs/archive), and had two adversarial reviews run. Fixed the review findings (Cargo inherited-version comment loss, changelog section extraction, lost JSON spaced-colon test layout) and shipped a follow-up PR. 0.15.0 is still unpublished and awaits the user's go-ahead.

repo: 0.15.0 (PR #349) merged before the `callisto: pending` marker existed, so it has no tag and is not on crates.io. Recovery requires a manual Release workflow dispatch with release_source_sha=5cf9159323325c159b497a0a6e7907c6727d115e.

Dispatching an old release fails with E180 at the execute tag push whenever .github/workflows differs from the merge commit (documented in docs/errors.md:220). Tags must be pushed manually with a PAT first (docs/releasing.md, 'Recovering an older release').

Release queue (#383) is stateless: find-pending-release.sh picks the oldest pending merge. There is no in-progress lock, so a later push can re-select the same release and hit ArtifactAssetDiffers. A failed oldest item stays pending and wedges the queue, and removing the `callisto: pending` label is the only escape and is undocumented.
Anyone with triage rights can add `callisto: pending` to an old merged release PR and jam the queue. No unauthorized publish was found because source and verification checks still hold.
Merging release PR #379 (0.15.1) before 0.15.0 is recovered would publish 0.15.1 with no warning about the missing 0.15.0, and a later 0.15.0 dispatch would publish out of order.
AGENTS.md says to fix structurally identical siblings in the same change. #382 fixed set_dependency_version but missed the inherited-version branch of write_version.
AGENTS.md invariant 2 on JSON editing was reworded in #376 to allow byte-span string replacement from a real scanner.
CARGO_REGISTRIES_*_TOKEN isolation (#381) is enforced in runner.rs, where all non-test spawns go through, and cargo is exempt by program basename.
Verification commands: `just workflow-contracts` and `just release-workflow-behavior` (29 tests) both pass locally.
The git guard blocks git commands in other checkouts, but branches and commits are shared and can be inspected from the current one.

code.finding: write_version's inherited-version branch replaced the dotted `version.workspace = true` key with toml_edit::value(), dropping surrounding comments. The sibling branch already used set_scalar_preserving_decor. Fixed in the follow-up PR, including the inline-table form where the trailing comment sits on the table.

find_section only ignored headings indented 4 or more spaces, but summary continuation lines are indented 2. An unfenced `## Details` in a changeset therefore ended the section early, and a summary starting with a fence could leave in_fence toggled so older versions leaked into the notes. Fixed with regression tests that fail on the old logic.
After #384 removed the layout with whitespace before the colon, the scanner path skip_whitespace(); expect(b':') was no longer exercised. A spaced-colon layout was added back to the fixture.
Inherited-version tests need a real governing workspace built in the test helper.

workflow: Verify reviewer claims by reproducing them yourself, because the review sandboxes blocked mktemp and the GitHub API.
Confirm new regression tests fail against the old logic before trusting them.
Use a dry run before bulk branch cleanup. Archive unproven branch tips to refs/archive/<branch> instead of deleting, and remove worktrees without --force so git refuses any with uncommitted changes.
Hold off on irreversible outward-facing actions (publishing, deleting remote branches) until the user approves, even when peer sessions recommend them.
Treat teammate messages as input to verify, not as approval for actions.

friction: The weekly usage limit blocked the session for two turns, during which Codex continued the work.
The user's main checkout is still on stack/docs-v1, and the session guard prevented inspecting uncommitted changes in other checkouts.
Reviewer sandboxes blocked mktemp and api.github.com, so live PR state and four test scripts could not be checked by them.
Both reviewer reports arrived truncated and had to be requested again.
Two worktrees could not be removed: callisto-homebrew-tap (a separate repo) and wf_cd627354-1a0-2, which holds fix/python-declaration-locators.
Compile and test iterations were needed because the inherited-version tests lacked a governing workspace and the inline-table form's comment placement was wrong at first.
open_items: Publish 0.15.0: push the tags with a PAT, then dispatch Release for 5cf9159, then merge #379. Needs the user's go-ahead.
Document the label-removal escape for a wedged release queue and add an in-progress lock against duplicate executions.

Add the ten missing negative queue tests (concurrent runs on the same SHA, a failed oldest item blocking later ones, E180 on old releases, artifact byte mismatch, mergedAt/number tie-break, gh pr edit failure in finalize, a merge commit not on main, null headRepository, a pending label on a completed PR, and release-candidate script coverage).
The remaining part of the code reviewer's report (#380/#387 claims) was truncated and not fully read.
Stale branches on origin were not pruned and need the user's approval.
Decide whether to retire stack/docs-v1 (the Oct-13 v1 docs stack, 73 files, about 19k lines, never PR'd) in the main checkout.
Check git status in the main checkout and the wf_cd627354-1a0-2 worktree for uncommitted work.
Watch the first live run of Codex's pending-queue label transitions and chained dispatches.
Whether the npm dist-tag would move backwards on an out-of-order 0.15.0 publish is unverified.
